rounds.text: NTC Industries Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation of 9.28x P/E and 0.90x price-to-book value, sitting at just 8% of its 52-week range despite robust compounding [E1, E2, E5]. The company has demonstrated impressive long-term and accelerating top-line expansion, led by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 20% and trailing twelve months sales growth reaching 36% [E14, E17]. Furthermore, profitability is scaling efficiently alongside revenue, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 27%, 3-year profit growth of 46%, and operating margins expanding to 26% in June 2026 compared to 20% in the year-ago quarter [E18, E20, E31]. Operational efficiency is also improving as debtor days have shortened from 58.0 to 35.0 days, while borrowings have been reduced to Rs 77 Cr [E39, E54]. Institutional interest is validating this turnaround, with foreign institutions increasing their stake to 5.67% and overall money flow registering as positive [E42, E44]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -8 Cr for March 2026 and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E35].

The company presents severe cash generation red flags, demonstrated by operating cash flow collapsing to negative ₹ 8 Cr and free cash flow dropping to negative ₹ 10 Cr in March 2026, alongside a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.40x [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain coincides with a staggering ballooning of working capital days from 57.5 days to 219 days [E60], pointing to severe operational inefficiencies beneath the reported earnings. Furthermore, reported profits are compromised by a reliance on non-operating sources, specifically including ₹ 11.4 Cr of other income [E58]. Insiders are voting with their feet as promoter holdings have dropped significantly by 11.56 percentage points since September 2023 down to 54.34% [E41, E59]. Compounded share price performance reflects this underlying malaise, showing a 1-year decline of -27% and a 5-year stagnation of -1% [E23, E25]. Finally, capital efficiency remains subpar with a 3-year median return on equity of just 8% [E28] and an overall ROE of 9.3% [E13], failing to reward shareholders who also receive a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong historical sales and profit growth alongside an expansion in operating margins [E16, E20, E30].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to negative ₹ 8 Cr and free cash flow to negative ₹ 10 Cr in March 2026 alongside a cash conversion of -0.40x [E34, E35, E36]. However, this cash drain occurs alongside comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.33x and a slight reduction in overall borrowings down to ₹ 77 Cr [E38, E39]. Conceded: working capital days increased and other income stands at ₹ 11.4 Cr [E58, E60], but the core business demonstrates powerful top-line momentum with 36% TTM compounded sales growth and an operating margin expanding to 20% from 12% three years prior [E17, E30]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased by 11.56 percentage points to 54.34% [E41], but institutional money flow is positive with foreign institutions increasing their stake by 5.65 percentage points [E42, E44]. Conceded: the 3-year median ROE is 8% and dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E28], yet the stock trades at an exceptionally low P/E of 9.28x and P/B of 0.90x compared to sector benchmarks of 17.61x and 2.18x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Finally, the negative 1-year price performance of -27% [E25] simply reflects stale sentiment that ignores accelerating earnings, quarterly profit growth, and expanding margins [E63, E64, E65, E67].

Conceded: the current ratio sits at a comfortable 3.33x and borrowings decreased slightly to ₹ 77 Cr [E38, E39]; however, liquidity buffers offer little comfort when cash generation turns deeply negative with operating and free cash flows plunging to ₹ -8 Cr and ₹ -10 Cr respectively [E35, E36]. Conceded: TTM sales grew 36% and operating margins expanded [E17, E30], yet reported earnings are inflated by ₹ 11.4 Cr of other income [E58], and quarterly sales actually dropped 10% year-on-year [E66]. Conceded: foreign institutions increased their stake by 5.65 percentage points [E42], but total promoter ownership dropped significantly by 11.56 percentage points [E41]. Conceded: headline multiples look cheap at 9.28x P/E and 0.90x P/B [E1, E2], but low valuations are justified by a depressed 3-year median ROE of 8% [E28] and a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Finally, blaming stale sentiment for the -27% one-year price drop [E25] ignores fundamental deterioration, notably working capital days ballooning from 57.5 to 219 days [E60].
